title: Taiwanese American Student Association at UC Santa Barbara
content_html:
The Taiwanese American Student Association (TASA) at UC Santa Barbara is a student-led social and cultural organization that celebrates and explores Taiwanese American culture. Officially recognized on UCSB’s Shoreline platform and listed by the university’s Asian Resource Center and Undergraduate Admissions office, TASA is open to students of all cultural backgrounds and describes its mission as fostering community, friendship, and cultural awareness through events, workshops, and service initiatives.

TASA is best known for its Annual Night Market, held each spring at Storke Plaza, which has grown into one of the most prominent student-run cultural events on campus. The event brings together a wide range of UCSB’s Asian Pacific Islander organizations and features food, performances, and games. Press coverage from the Daily Nexus and The Bottom Line confirms the Night Market was in its 14th year in 2019, its 17th in 2023 (the first full return to Storke Plaza after COVID-19), and its 20th in 2025 — placing the event’s origins around 2005 or 2006, though an exact founding year for TASA itself has not been confirmed in first-party sources. In addition to the Night Market, TASA organizes a Big & Little mentorship pairing program, seasonal retreats, shaved ice socials, and other community events throughout the academic year.

TASA maintains an active web presence across multiple platforms, including a primary website at ucsbtsa.com, an Instagram account (@tasa.ucsb) with over 2,100 followers, a Facebook page, and a Linktree. The organization’s FAQ distinguishes it from the co-existing Taiwanese Student Association (TSA), noting that TASA focuses on the Taiwanese American experience while TSA primarily serves Taiwanese international students.
